summary: This Part II of RankZeroOneBSD plans the all-prime rank-zero converse for CM newforms and CM elliptic curves, and its twist-nonvanishing applications. The proof passes through rational Poitou–Tate, central cyclotomic specialization, the actual Beilinson–Kato class and reciprocity. Completed coefficient and dyadic conventions are explicit. The congruent-number application has an exact half-density after an ordering comparison; the CM twist and non-descent applications have lower proportion at least one half. This is a complete target-level planning pass, not a closed proof or implementation: all stages are planned, supplier requests and two missing registered inputs are explicit.

nodes.title: The rank-r p-converse proposition
nodes.statement: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ, a prime p and r ∈ ℕ, pConverse(E,p,r) is the proposition corank_{ℤ_p} Sel_{p∞}(E/ℚ)=r ⇒ analyticRank(E)=r. The analytic rank is the finite order at 1 of the actual arithmetic L-function, not of a freely chosen analytic germ.
hypotheses: E is elliptic over ℚ; p is prime; the Selmer module is cofinitely generated as in its supplier.
proofSteps: Use the existing p∞ Selmer group, its corank and the existing analytic rank; introduce only the implication.
acceptance: The predicate is meaningful at every prime, including 2; its definition proves no rank-r theorem.

sources.match: The rank-r implication fixes the direction, the corank and the analytic conclusion.

nodes.title: Kato’s cohomological realization at the centre
nodes.statement: For a normalized newform f of level N≥1 and even weight k≥2, coefficient field F and λ|p, use E=F_λ and M_f=V_Kato(f)=ρ_f^∨. Put h=k/2, W=M_f(h), and W′=W^∨(1). Kato’s conjugate form f* satisfies M_{f*}≅M_f^∨(1−k), so W′≅M_{f*}(h). Both are de Rham at p; complex conjugation has one eigenline of each sign. At good ℓ≠p the geometric-Frobenius polynomial of M_f is X²−a_ℓ(f)X+ε_f(ℓ)ℓ^(k−1).
hypotheses: All realizations and coefficient embeddings are the ones of R19.1; the fixed newform carrier is the baseline Newform, not a newly defined form.
proofSteps: Read R19.1’s cohomological/arithmetic dictionary and apply Kato (14.10.1). Dualize and twist explicitly. Use R19.5 for the classical coefficient-prime statement without an ordinarity or p∤N restriction.
acceptance: For a weight-two modular elliptic curve with trivial character, M_f(1) is its rational Tate module via the Weil pairing; M_f alone is its dual.

nodes.title: Global invariants of modular twists vanish
nodes.statement: For every normalized cuspidal newform f of weight k≥2, every coefficient place λ and integer r, H⁰(ℚ,M_f(r))=0. In particular H⁰(ℚ,W)=H⁰(ℚ,W′)=0 at the even-weight centre.
hypotheses: The realization is the actual irreducible two-dimensional newform realization.
proofSteps: Apply classical newform irreducibility after the dual and Tate twist; a nonzero invariant line would contradict irreducibility. At even weight the good-prime weight bound also excludes eigenvalue 1.
acceptance: No assertion is made that all local invariants vanish for arbitrary twists; only the central local statement below is used.

nodes.title: Finite-level H² vanishes under Selmer zero
nodes.statement: If H¹_f(ℚ,W)=0 then H²(Z[1/p],j_*T(h))[1/p]=0 for any stable lattice T⊂M_f, in Kato’s étale convention. Here j_* retains the prescribed local extension at bad primes; changing the ramification set without its local corrections is forbidden.
hypotheses: Even k≥2; W=M_f(h), W′=M_{f*}(h); modular local cohomology has dim H¹(ℚ_p,W)=2, dim H¹_f(ℚ_p,W)=1 and H⁰=H²=0, also for W′.
proofSteps: First apply rational Poitou–Tate (Kato 14.9.3) to W′. Its Tate-dual finite Selmer term is zero by H¹_f(ℚ,W)=0, and local H²(ℚ_p,W′)=0; exactness therefore gives global H²(W′)=0 and an isomorphism H¹(W′)/H¹_f(W′)≅H¹(ℚ_p,W′)/H¹_f(ℚ_p,W′). The right side has dimension one. The finite difference between Kato’s S(T) and the classical finite Selmer group disappears after rationalization.
Global H⁰(W′)=0 and the Euler identity h⁰−h¹+h²=−1 now give dim H¹(W′)=1. Since its quotient by H¹_f(W′) also has dimension one, H¹_f(ℚ,W′)=0.
Apply the same Poitou–Tate sequence to W. Its Tate-dual finite Selmer term now vanishes, and H²(ℚ_p,W)=0, giving the asserted global H² vanishing.
At p=2 retain real-place Tate terms and the integral errors killed by 2 through both applications. Only then invert p.
acceptance: Both appearances of the Tate dual and the rationalization at 2 are displayed; Selmer zero is not substituted for its dual without proof.

proofSteps: Use R19.3/R19.5 and Kato (14.10.4)–(14.10.5) for f*: each eigenvalue of φ on D_cris(W′) has complex absolute value p^(−1/2) or p^(−1), when present. At a monodromic bad prime use the weight on ker N, not a claim that every invariant has weight −1. Thus D_cris(W′)^{φ=1}=0.
Apply the supplied formula dim H_g−dim H_f=dim D_cris(W′)^{φ=1}, the inclusion H_f⊆H_g and ker exp*=H_g. Use the modular local dimensions for the quotient dimension.
acceptance: The result includes p|N. For a general de Rham representation H_g can exceed H_f, so the Frobenius calculation is a required hypothesis check.

nodes.title: Control at the negative half-weight character
nodes.statement: Apply SI L3 rational specialization at 𝔮 to Kato’s actual Iwasawa complex. If H¹_f(ℚ,W)=0, then H²_Iw(M_f)_𝔮=0 and H¹_Iw(M_f)_𝔮/𝔮 ≅ H¹(Z[1/p],j_*T(h))[1/p]. The identification is the semilinear twist by h followed by finite-level evaluation.
hypotheses: Kato’s complex, local extension convention and compatible induced local conditions agree with the SI complex; finite generation and rational amplitude ≤2 hold.
proofSteps: Import derived control, not an underived quotient assertion. In degree one retain 0→H¹_Iw/𝔮→H¹_finite→Tor₁^A(H²_Iw,E)→0 on the selected component.

In degree two retain the possible Tor₁(H³_Iw,E) until the amplitude theorem removes it. Then H²_Iw,𝔮/𝔮 ≅ H²_finite=0; finite generation and Nakayama give H²_Iw,𝔮=0. Its degree-one Tor term vanishes, yielding the stated isomorphism.
For p=2 pass to the appropriate rational Δ idempotent before the procyclic computation. The kernel is ev_h, never ev_{−h}.
acceptance: This node specializes an imported control theorem; it owns no second generic control construction. A proof that discards H²[𝔮] before the degree-two calculation is rejected.

nodes.title: The specialized Kato class is a basis
nodes.statement: Assume H¹_f(ℚ,W)=0 and the rational Kato equality char_A H²_Iw(M_f)=char_A(H¹_Iw(M_f)/Z(f)), with H¹_Iw free of rank one and H²_Iw torsion. If γ^{centralSign(k)}≠0, then centralZeta(f,λ,γ) is an E-basis of the global cohomology line.

Use the Kato conjugation relation, ev_h(σ_{−1})=(−1)^h, and the one-dimensional c-eigenspaces. The wrong eigenspace dies in the selected component; any γ with nonzero ε projection generates Z_𝔮. Reduce modulo 𝔮 and apply the control isomorphism.

nodes.title: Reciprocity detects the central L-value
nodes.statement: If loc_p(centralZeta(f,λ,γ)) is not in H¹_f(ℚ_p,W), then L(f,k/2)≠0.
hypotheses: Even k≥2 and every p; use the actual arithmetic newform L-function and Kato’s coefficient/period embeddings.
proofSteps: The central H_g=H_f theorem makes exp*(loc_p centralZeta(γ)) nonzero. Choose an F-basis γ₁,γ₂ of the Hecke-field realization, whose extension to E=F_λ is M_f. The zeta morphism, twist-specialization, localization and dual exponential are E-linear; consequently at least one γᵢ has nonzero regulator. Apply Kato’s complex period formula to that F-rational γᵢ, not directly to an arbitrary completed-coefficient vector γ.

At r=h and the trivial finite character, the twist is k−r=h and the period projection is (2πi)^(h−1)L^{(p)}(f*,h)γᵢ^{(−1)^(h−1)}. The period comparison on the designated line is an isomorphism, so a nonzero regulator forces L^{(p)}(f*,h)≠0.

Use L^{(p)}(f*,s)=P_p(f*,p^(−s))L(f*,s), with every bad local factor retained. Nonvanishing of this product implies L(f*,h)≠0. Then L(f*,h)=overline{L(f,h)} under the chosen complex embedding. No division by a possibly zero Euler factor is needed for this implication.
acceptance: The critical value lies in the range 1≤h≤k−1. An unrestricted assertion ker exp*=H_f is not used.

The statement allows γ∈M_f over E=F_λ; its proof reduces to F-rational basis vectors before using complex periods. No scalar embedding F_λ→ℂ or complex period map on arbitrary completed scalars is assumed.

nodes.title: Typed CM Selmer and modular comparison
nodes.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic and E/K have CM by any order O⊂K. Choose a finite extension L/ℚ_p containing both embeddings of K and the theta-form coefficient fields. Write V_pE⊗L=η⊕η̄ via the two CM coefficient idempotents, with η̄=η^∨(1) from the Weil pairing. For the weight-two theta forms f_η and f_{η̄}, M_{f_η}⊗L≅Ind_{G_K}^{G_ℚ}η^∨, so M_{f_η}(1)⊗L≅Ind η̄, and conversely for f_{η̄}. Kummer, coefficient extension and finite-condition Shapiro give H¹_f(K,V_pE)⊗L≅H¹_f(ℚ,M_{f_η}(1)⊗L)⊕H¹_f(ℚ,M_{f_{η̄}}(1)⊗L), up to the indicated order of the two summands. Consequently corank Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=0 implies both modular finite Selmer spaces vanish.
hypotheses: All endomorphisms are defined over K; coefficients are completed p-adic fields, not K used as a scalar extension of a ℤ_p module. There is no integral rank-one freeness at conductor primes.
proofSteps: Use SI’s exact Kummer/Bloch–Kato comparison: H¹_f(K,V_pE)=(lim_m Sel_{p^m},[p])[1/p], zero iff the p∞ corank is zero. This is a Tate-module comparison, not an unidentified isomorphism with the Pontryagin dual.

Use CM.4’s actual Hecke character and rational coefficient decomposition. Apply the requested theta/induction extension of CM.4; its current cm-induction-comparison node only treats E/ℚ and does not suffice for a twist over K which does not descend.

Apply compact Shapiro, its local Mackey decomposition and the supplied finite-condition compatibility at every place, including places over p. Extend to L and use faithful coefficient extension to reflect vanishing.
acceptance: Check p=2,K=ℚ(i), including the order of conductor 2; check ramified p=3,K=ℚ(ζ₃). The comparison requires neither descent to ℚ nor maximal CM order.

nodes.title: CM Selmer corank doubles over the CM field
nodes.statement: If E/ℚ has CM by an order of K, then for every p, corank Sel_{p∞}(E/K)=2·corank Sel_{p∞}(E/ℚ).
hypotheses: K is its imaginary quadratic CM field; E_K denotes base change.
proofSteps: Use the parent odd-primary Selmer decomposition when p≠2, and its two-primary restriction/corestriction maps when p=2. After rationalizing duals they identify the K-corank with the sum of the coranks for E and E^{χ_K} over ℚ.

Use CM.1’s rational self-twist isogeny E→E^{χ_K}, then the imported ELL7 isogeny-corank comparison to identify the two summands. The rational projectors (1±σ)/2 are permitted over ℚ_2; they assert no integral splitting.
acceptance: At p=2 retain the finite kernels and cokernels killed by 2 before rationalization. The self-twist is an isogeny, not generally an isomorphism.

nodes.title: CM analytic order doubles over the CM field
nodes.statement: If E/ℚ has CM by an order of K, then ord_{s=1} L(E/K,s)=2·analyticRank(E/ℚ).
hypotheses: Use the unique analytic continuations of the actual arithmetic Euler products.
proofSteps: Use the self-twist isogeny and equality of all Euler factors of isogenous curves to identify L(E^{χ_K},s)=L(E,s). Apply the parent quadratic base-change factorization and order-additivity theorem. Thus the entire base-change L-function is the square of L(E,s), independent of the rank.

nodes.title: The even parity Goldfeld proposition
nodes.statement: For an elliptic curve E/ℚ, EvenGoldfeld(E) asserts that the proportion of fundamental discriminants d with 0<|d|≤X and L(E^{(d)},1)≠0 tends to 1/2 as X→∞. Count both signs, once each and without stabilizer weights. The trivial quadratic character, represented by d=1 when included by the arithmetic convention, changes only a finite set.
hypotheses: Use ST.0’s arithmetic family, counting and relative density, and the parent actual quadratic twists and L-functions.
proofSteps: Restrict the existing absolute-discriminant family to the analytic-rank-zero subset and use relative density 1/2. Introduce no new density or fundamental-discriminant carrier.
acceptance: Positive squarefree parameters are a different height presentation; converting to this proposition requires the comparison theorem below.

nodes.statement: Let E:y²=x³−x and S(X)={n∈ℕ:0<n≤X, n squarefree, n≡1,2,3 mod 8}. Then #{n∈S(X):L(E^{(n)}/ℚ,1)≠0}/#S(X)→1.

proofSteps: Apply the all-prime CM elliptic converse at p=2 to every twist in the density-one corank-zero subset. The twist remains CM by ℤ[i]. Inclusion of this subset in the analytic-rank-zero set and the upper bound 1 squeeze its relative density to 1.
acceptance: The input is 2∞ Selmer corank, not dim Sel_2; the positive restriction is explicit.

nodes.title: Exactly half of positive squarefree twists have rank zero
nodes.statement: For E:y²=x³−x and P(X)={0<n≤X:n squarefree}, #{n∈P(X):L(E^{(n)},1)≠0}/#P(X)→1/2.
hypotheses: Use the root-number computation for positive squarefree n and the functional-equation parity theorem.
proofSteps: By the parent root-number calculation, every positive squarefree twist outside residues 1,2,3 mod 8 has sign −1 and vanishes at 1. Thus the zero-rank set is contained in S. Apply the ST.0 density-one-to-half comparison to congruent-even-nonvanishing.

nodes.title: Goldfeld for the congruent-number curve
nodes.statement: For E:y²=x³−x, EvenGoldfeld(E) holds for fundamental discriminants of both signs ordered by |d|.
hypotheses: For a positive squarefree n write d_+(n) for the fundamental discriminant of ℚ(√n) and d_−(n) for that of ℚ(√−n), with the trivial class handled finitely.
proofSteps: Use E^{(−n)}≅E^{(n)} and identify the character twist for d with the twist by its signed squarefree part. By ST.0’s squarefree residue counts the six residues 1,2,3,5,6,7 mod 8 each have count X/π²+o(X).

For odd n the two |d| cutoffs use multipliers 1 and 4; for even squarefree n both use 4. Summing inverse multipliers, the root-number-positive residues 1,2,3 have weight 5/4+1/2+5/4=3, and all residues have weight 6.

Restrict density one to each positive-density residue class, apply ST.0’s piecewise rescaling theorem, and use the root-number upper bound. The resulting zero-rank proportion for the discriminant ordering is exactly 3/6.
acceptance: A bound only for positive fundamental discriminants does not match the proposition. Check n=2 gives d=±8 and n=3 gives d=12,−3.

Apply cm-elliptic-k at p=3 to the corank-zero subset. Monotonicity of counts gives the same lower bound for the nonzero-value subset.

nodes.title: The cube-sum Weierstrass model
nodes.statement: For n∈ℤ define cubeSumModel(n) to be the existing WeierstrassCurve over ℚ with coefficients (a₁,a₂,a₃,a₄,a₆)=(0,0,0,0,−27n²), so Y²=X³−27n². The definition is total, but its elliptic applications require n≠0. This is a model for the smooth projective completion of x³+y³=2n with origin [1:−1:0].
hypotheses: Characteristic zero. The projective cubic and its origin belong to the existing elliptic-curve model comparison interface.
proofSteps: Give the five coefficients on Mathlib’s WeierstrassCurve carrier. For n≠0 use the projective linear map [x:y:z]↦[6nz:9n(x−y):x+y], with inverse [X:Y:Z]↦[9nZ+Y:9nZ−Y:3X]. Their composites are the scalar 18n. If F=x³+y³−2nz³ and G=Y²Z−X³+27n²Z³, substitution gives G(forward)=108n²F and F(inverse)=54nG, verifying the claimed projective cubic equation. On the chart x+y≠0 this is X=6n/(x+y), Y=9n(x−y)/(x+y).
acceptance: The chosen scale gives −27n² rather than −432n²; both are isomorphic by X↦4X,Y↦8Y in the conventional model.

proofSteps: Use the discriminant and projective model comparison. The automorphism (X,Y)↦(ζ₃X,Y) fixes the origin, satisfies 1+ζ₃+ζ₃²=0 in the endomorphism ring and gives the full CM ring ℤ[ζ₃] (already maximal). Use disc K=−3 and (3)=𝔭², then apply cm-twist-nonvanishing.

nodes.title: Parameters of twists descending to ℚ
nodes.statement: For any elliptic E/K over an imaginary quadratic K=ℚ(√D), let D_E={t∈K×/K×²:E^{(t)} is K-isomorphic to the base change of an elliptic curve over ℚ}. If nonempty, D_E is contained in a union of at most two cosets of the image of ℚ×/ℚ×². If j(E)≠1728 one coset suffices; for j=1728 representatives can be chosen t₀ and t₀√D for any one descending parameter t₀.
hypotheses: Descending means descent as a pointed elliptic curve; neither descent of a chosen equation nor of its CM action is required.
proofSteps: Choose one descending twist E₀/ℚ and compare all others to its base change. For j≠0,1728, use the existing quadratic twist classification and the fact that two ℚ-curves of this j are rational quadratic twists.
For j=0 use models Y²=X³+B with B∈ℚ×. If B·u³/B′ is a sixth power in K, then [u]³ is trivial in K×/(ℚ×K×²); this quotient has exponent 2, so [u] is trivial. Thus all parameters lie in one coset.

For j=1728 use Y²=X³+AX with A∈ℚ×. Isomorphism requires u²∈ℚ×K×⁴. Hence u/v² has square in ℚ, and is rational or rational times √D. This gives the two cosets. If there is no descending twist the set is empty.
acceptance: Treat the exceptional automorphism cases explicitly. No assertion that E itself descends is needed, and j=1728 is not treated as an injective twist parametrization.

sources.match: The non-descent consequence requires a parameter count; this algebraic reduction supplies its first step.

nodes.title: Descending twists have height density zero
nodes.statement: For fixed E/K with K imaginary quadratic, # {t∈D_E:H(t)<X}=O_{E,K}(√X). As # {t∈K×/K×²:H(t)<X}∼c_K X with c_K>0, descending twists have H-density zero.
hypotheses: Use the exact odd-valuation support height, not the norm of a chosen representative or the relative discriminant height. The total squareclass asymptotic is requested from ST.0.
proofSteps: For a fixed coset a·im(ℚ×/ℚ×²), represent the rational part by signed squarefree integers n. Outside the finitely many primes dividing disc K and the odd support of a, a rational prime dividing n contributes ℓ² to H_K([n]), whether split or inert. Ramified rational primes contribute only a fixed finite ambiguity, and multiplication by a changes height by bounded factors from its fixed support.

Thus H_K(a[n]) is bounded below by a positive constant times n_outside²; there are O(√X) rational squarefree parameters, even allowing the finite ambiguity and duplicate images. Apply descending-twist-cosets.

Divide by the ST.0 positive linear asymptotic. Its proof uses finite support-ideal fibers and squarefree ideal counts in the square ideal-class subgroup, not an assumption that every squarefree ideal is principal.
acceptance: For a rational prime unramified in K, height is ℓ², not ℓ. The finite kernel of the rational squareclass map cannot enlarge this upper bound.

sources.match: A zero-density count makes the asserted non-descent proportion quantitative.
Its support height is the ordering used in this count.

nodes.title: Non-descending twists with analytic rank zero
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of cm-twist-nonvanishing, liminf_{X→∞} #{t:H(t)<X,E^{(t)} does not descend to ℚ,L(E^{(t)}/K,1)≠0}/#{t:H(t)<X}≥1/2. The same lower bound holds with the denominator restricted to non-descending twists.
hypotheses: Each squareclass is counted once; the denominator is eventually nonzero and tends to infinity.
proofSteps: Subtract the O(√X) descending set from the numerator supplied by cm-twist-nonvanishing and divide by the linear total count. The removed ratio tends to zero, and the restricted denominator has ratio tending to 1.
acceptance: This strengthens “positive proportion” only to a lower bound ≥1/2, not to an exact density. It does not count different presentations of the same curve with new weights.

sources.match: The nonvanishing proposition still supplies a positive proportion after removing the thin descending family.

Supply the p-omitted identity L^{(p)}(f*,s)=P_p(f*,p^(−s))L(f*,s), using the correct local factor at p|N, and compatibility of theta-form L-functions with Hecke-character L-functions.

For every number field F, isogeny φ:E→E′ and prime p, maps on classical Kummer Sel_{p∞} preserve all local images. Their composites with the dual-isogeny maps are multiplication by deg φ. Their finite kernels/cokernels vanish after rationalizing Pontryagin duals, so the coranks agree, including p|deg φ. The existing characteristic-zero quadratic twist and pointed-model comparison interfaces must include exceptional j=0,1728 forms: j=0 coefficients modulo sixth powers and j=1728 coefficients modulo fourth powers. The existing finite-module global-euler-characteristic node is not by itself this rational statement.

Prove it with the non-exceptional specialization consequence of Theorem 12.5(3), printed p. 222, retaining the k=2 local-H² exception κ^(−2)χ and checking that the central character κ^(−1) is different. Independent CM weak Leopoldt and free rank-one/torsion Iwasawa structure must precede construction/use of zeta classes; Kato 15.13–15.17 is the route, not equality inferred from a conjecture that already uses the zeta map.

Apply the existing generic derived-control theorem to Kato’s actual j_* cyclotomic complex, with the same bad-prime local extension. Supply finite generation and rational amplitude ≤2, the degree-one Tor₁(H²,E) and degree-two Tor₁(H³,E) sequences, and compatibility with Tw_h followed by augmentation. For Λ=O[[Gal(ℚ(μ_{p∞})/ℚ)]] and A=Λ[1/p], supply continuous evaluation σ_c↦c^(−h), residue A/𝔮≅E and the DVR A_𝔮 on its selected rational finite-character component; retain Δ={±1} at p=2 until rational idempotents can be used. Use the existing completed group algebra, not a direct group-ring substitute.

At ℓ≠p, compare Kato j_*T cohomology with the finite Bloch–Kato local condition for central modular W, including every bad prime. Use the modular local eigenvalue bounds to remove the rational unramified/inertia obstruction; integral Tamagawa terms may persist. Kummer gives H¹_f(F,V_pE)=T_p Sel_{p∞}(E/F)⊗ℚ_p, not an untyped Pontryagin-dual isomorphism. The existing elliptic-finite-kummer is reused, not reconstructed.

For L containing both embeddings, V_pE⊗L=η⊕η̄ and η̄=η^∨(1). Construct the actual normalized theta forms with M_{f_η}⊗L≅Ind η^∨ and hence M_{f_η}(1)⊗L≅Ind η̄. Identify their arithmetic L-functions with L(ψ_η/K,s) and L(ψ_{η̄}/K,s), including conductor primes, so their product is the existing full L(E/K,s). Current CM.4/cm-induction-comparison assumes E/ℚ and does not supply this general case. Rational decomposition suffices at order-index primes.

For the explicit j=0 cube-sum model, use the existing endomorphism/CM interface to identify (X,Y)↦(ζ₃X,Y) with an injective ℤ[ζ₃] action. This order is maximal, so the characteristic-zero elliptic endomorphism classification gives full CM; export disc ℚ(ζ₃)=−3 and ramification of 3. Reuse the existing CM-order/isogeny theory for nonmaximal-order statistical reduction.

Export the fundamental-discriminant family and finite-change/relative-density rules used in EvenGoldfeld, with both signs and |d| height.
